title: Canons 6–8: pious taste hell's pains tempered; impious carry hell daily; broad way
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): (8) The way ye which most pursue stands as ye way belonging toward hell, ye which ye more it stands as loved ye more it ought to be suspect to ye pious. || (7) The impious, although they carry their hell about together with them daily in this life, yet most rarely feel it because belonging toward incredible stupor, plus under it at last they sink. || Christ felt ye pains belonging toward hell in our place. (6) The pious in this life sometimes also feel some belonging toward hell's torments, ye which yet God's grace so tempers such that they make them seek him more ardently.
pass_b_english: (6) The pious in this life sometimes also feel some of hell's torments, which yet God's grace so tempers that they make them seek him more ardently. Christ felt the pains of hell in our place.
(7) The impious, although they carry their hell about with them daily in this life, yet most rarely feel it because of incredible stupor, and under it at last they sink.
(8) The way which most pursue is the way of hell, which the more it is loved the more it ought to be suspect to the pious.
source_text: 6. Pii in hac vita nonnunquam etiam inferni cruciatus aliquos persentiunt, quos tamen Dei gratia ita temperat ut ad ipsum ardentius quaerendum faciant. Christus dolores inferorum nostro loco sensit. 7. Impii quamvis infernum suum in hac vita quotidie secum circumferant, rarissime tamen prae incredibili stupore sentiunt, & sub eo tandem succumbunt. 8. Via quam plurimi sectantur via inferni est, quae quo magis amatur eo magis suspecta esse debet piis.
